table_title: For each decade of the 20th century (1900s through 1990s), list five major technological or scientific milestones with their attributed individual or organization and country of origin.
db_analog: SELECT decade, list_position, milestone, attributed_to, country FROM twentieth_century_milestones WHERE decade IN ('1900s','1910s','1920s','1930s','1940s','1950s','1960s','1970s','1980s','1990s') ORDER BY decade, list_position
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-decade and per-event articles accessed 2026-04-29. Decade universe is fixed (the 10 decades of the 20th century, 1900s-1990s). Per-decade selections are anchored to that decade's Wikipedia overview article. Schema cycle-2 audit renames: column 'Invention' -> 'Milestone' and column 'Inventor' -> 'Attributed To' to match the cycle-1 broadened framing from 'inventions' to 'technological or scientific milestones'. Composite PK is (Decade, Milestone) with List Position as a non-key numeric display ordinal recording the curator's documented display order for each decade. 20th-century milestones are stable historical facts and do not drift on a multi-year timescale, but the article snapshots on which the attribution values rely may be edited; nearly every row has an explicit per-event Wikipedia article cited in source_urls so the row attribution is article-traceable.
_extraction_notes: Universe: the 10 decades of the 20th century (1900s through 1990s). Per-decade selection convention: each decade's 'five major technological or scientific milestones' are drawn from the Wikipedia decade overview article's most-emphasized entries, supplemented by per-event/per-organization Wikipedia articles where the per-decade article does not name the principal individual or organization. The cycle-0 staging applies lessons from the world_religions_top5_holy_sites cycles 1-2 audits: (a) the table_title says 'list five major technological or scientific milestones' (selection, not ranked top-5; cycle-1 audit broadened 'inventions' to 'milestones' because some staged rows are discoveries rather than strict inventions — Nuclear fission 1939, DNA double-helix 1953 — or large-scale projects rather than single inventions — Manhattan Project / Trinity test 1945, Skylab 1973, Voyager Program 1977); (b) composite PK is (Decade, Milestone) with List Position as a non-key numeric column that records the curator's documented display order for each decade. The 'Attributed To' column (renamed from 'Inventor' at cycle-2 audit; cycle-1 broadened it semantically and cycle-2 renamed it for accuracy) may be: an individual (Wright Brothers, Theodore Maiman, Tim Berners-Lee), a multi-individual joint attribution (Bardeen & Brattain & Shockley, Crick & Watson, Eckert & Mauchly), or an organization (NASA, IBM, Sony, DARPA, Manhattan Project, OKB-1, CERN, Eastman Kodak, Japanese National Railways). Cycle-1 audit fixes: (i) inventor cell for Sputnik 1 changed from 'Sergei Korolev' to 'OKB-1 (Mikhail S. Khomyakov)' per the Sputnik 1 Wikipedia article's explicit 'chief constructor' attribution; (ii) Hydrogen bomb inventor changed from 'Edward Teller' to 'Edward Teller & Stanislaw Ulam (Teller-Ulam design)' per the Edward Teller article's documented co-inventor with Ulam; (iii) Walkman inventor changed from 'Sony (Masaru Ibuka)' to 'Sony (Nobutoshi Kihara)' because the Walkman article credits Ibuka with conceiving the idea but credits Kihara with the engineering work per the Nobutoshi Kihara Wikipedia article; (iv) Lithium-ion battery inventor changed from 'Sony' to 'Sony (using Akira Yoshino's design)' per the Lithium-ion battery article's explicit attribution; (v) ARPANET inventor changed from 'DARPA (Bob Taylor)' to 'DARPA' because Bob Taylor 'initiated the project in 1966' rather than inventing it. (vi) source_urls expanded across cycles 1 and 2: at cycle-1 from 12 to 27 (added ENIAC, Transistor, Microwave oven, Edward Teller, Sputnik 1, Light-emitting diode, ARPANET, Tōkaidō Shinkansen, Intel 4004, Altair 8800, Walkman, Nobutoshi Kihara, Lithium-ion battery, Gene therapy, Dolly (sheep)); at cycle-2 from 27 to 31 (added Watson-Crick paper article for DNA double-helix, IBM Personal Computer, Mac (computer), Large Hadron Collider) for rows whose attribution/country was not yet supported by the per-decade article alone. Cycle-2 also renamed the schema columns 'Invention' -> 'Milestone' and 'Inventor' -> 'Attributed To' to match the cycle-1 broadened framing. Result: 10 decades x 5 milestones = 50 rows x 5 columns, composite PK on (Decade, Milestone), 0 duplicate PKs. Country column ranges over 8 distinct countries (USA, UK, Germany, Italy, Poland, Switzerland, Soviet Union, Japan).
